## Problem A swarm's real limit is often not files or lanes but a shared, windowed capacity: a model provider's weekly quota, a rate-limit window, a pool of CI runners. `pm swarm` can lease an exclusive resource (`pm swarm resource … --action reserve`), but it has no notion of a counted capacity that drains over a window, so: - `pm swarm next` and `start` hand out lanes that the provider cannot finish. In one week of real orchestration, four long-running agents were stopped 40 to 80 minutes into a task by an exhausted provider window. Each left uncommitted or unpushed work and no record of why it stopped. - A stopped lane looks like a stale claim. `reclaim --stale-after` returns it to the pool, and the next agent starts again from the item text instead of from the previous agent's state. - The orchestrator's budget rule ("the forecast at the reset must stay under 100%, so run at most N lanes") lives in ad-hoc scripts and is invisible to the agents it constrains. ## Proposal: `pm swarm capacity` Counted, windowed capacities stored as pm items with append-only observations. No provider API is called by the package; the caller reports what it measured. | command | effect | | --- | --- | | `pm swarm capacity codex --action declare --limit 100 --unit percent --window 7d --resets-at ` | Declare a capacity and its window | | `pm swarm capacity codex --action observe --used 44 --source codexbar` | Append one observation; the read model derives elapsed share, burn rate and forecast at reset | | `pm swarm capacity codex` | Status: used, elapsed, forecast, admitted lane count under the policy bands, time to reset | | `pm swarm capacity codex --action policy --band "forecast<88=3" --band "forecast<95=2" --band "forecast<98=1" --else 0` | How many lanes may hold this capacity at once | | `pm swarm next --agent worker --capacity codex` / `start … --capacity codex` | Admission: bind the lane to the capacity, or refuse with `capacity_forecast_exceeded` or `capacity_exhausted` and name the next capacity in a declared fallback order (`--capacity ollama,codex`) | | `pm swarm interrupt task-id --agent worker --token 1 --reason capacity_exhausted --capacity ollama` | Record that the lane stopped for capacity, keep the claim fenced (not stale), and mark the capacity exhausted until its reset | | `pm swarm brief task-id --continuation --to worker-2 --token-budget 800` | Continuation packet for a different agent or provider: what the lane changed since the claim (linked files, synced paths, comments and tests in order), what the acceptance criteria still require, and the interruption record. Transfers ownership like `handoff` | ## Acceptance criteria - Works without Git; in Git, the continuation packet also lists the lane's commits and uncommitted paths. - Admission is atomic under concurrent `next` calls (two agents cannot take the last admitted slot); proven with a real multi-process test. - Forecast is derived from at least two observations in the current window; with fewer it is reported as unknown and the policy's `--else` applies. An observation older than a stated age is reported as stale, never silently used. - `reclaim --stale-after` does not reclaim an interrupted lane before its capacity resets or a continuation is taken. - Every refusal names the capacity, the measured values, the reset time and one runnable next command. - No secrets or provider credentials are read or stored; observations are numbers plus a free-text source label. - README section with a worked example, 100% coverage, npm and bun acceptance. ## Why here and not a new package A standalone budget package was rejected in the 2026-11-04 overlap audit. Capacity is a scheduling input for lanes, next to the existing exclusive `resource` leases, and the continuation packet is a variant of `brief` plus `handoff`. --- ### GitHub comments (1) > **@coderabbitai[bot]** (2026-11-24T10:28:03Z) > > > > >
